title: Scalar extension respects direct-image geometric exchange
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of finite commutative rings and let
$$\begin{array}{ccc}X'&\xrightarrow h&X\\ f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow g&Y\end{array}$$
be a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Use ordinary unbounded constant-ring module derived categories on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], with the canonical adjunctions $u_R^{-1}\dashv Ru_*^R$ for $R=A,B$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Write $S_T=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T:D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\to D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let
$\lambda_u:u_B^{-1}S_V\xrightarrow{\sim}S_Tu_A^{-1}$, for $u:T\to V$, be the canonical tensor inverse-image comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], sending the inverse image of $x\otimes b$ to $u^{-1}x\otimes b$ on K-flat representatives. Define $\chi_u:S_VRu_*^A\to Ru_*^BS_T$ to be the mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] of $\lambda_u$ under $u_A^{-1}\dashv Ru_*^A$ and $u_B^{-1}\dashv Ru_*^B$. Write $\operatorname{Ex}^R:g_R^{-1}Rf_*^R\to Rf'_*{}^Rh_R^{-1}$ for the ambient ringed exchange [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] for constant ring $R$. For every $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ the following equality holds in $D(Y'_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$:
$$Rf'_*{}^B(\lambda_{h,M})\circ\operatorname{Ex}^B_{S_XM}\circ g_B^{-1}(\chi_{f,M})
=\chi_{f',h_A^{-1}M}\circ S_{Y'}(\operatorname{Ex}^A_M)\circ\lambda_{g,Rf_*^AM}.$$
Both sides run from $g_B^{-1}S_YRf_*^AM$ to $Rf'_*{}^BS_{X'}h_A^{-1}M$. The equality is natural in $M$; no properness, boundedness, constructibility, Tor-amplitude or flatness hypothesis on $A\to B$ is imposed.

proof.text:
Every $N\in D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ has a K-flat resolution $P\to N$ with flat terms [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], $S_TN$ is represented by the termwise tensor $P\otimes_{A_T}B_T$, canonically independent of $P$; this complex is again K-flat with flat terms over $B_T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], for $u:T\to V$ the inverse image $u^{-1}P$ is again K-flat with flat terms, so $S_Tu_A^{-1}N$ is represented by $u^{-1}P\otimes B_T$, and by the item's normalization $\lambda_{u,N}$ is the class of the termwise sheaf isomorphism $u^{-1}(P\otimes B_V)\to u^{-1}P\otimes B_T$, $u^{-1}(x\otimes b)\mapsto u^{-1}x\otimes b$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] the composition isomorphisms $c$, hence the square isomorphisms $\theta^A_\square,\theta^B_\square$ built from them in [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange], are on such complexes the classes of the termwise canonical isomorphisms of inverse images. Hence for every $N\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, represented by $Q$, the two composites $f'^{-1}_Bg_B^{-1}S_YN\to S_{X'}h_A^{-1}f_A^{-1}N$,
$$(\lambda_hf_A^{-1})\circ(h_B^{-1}\lambda_f)\circ(\theta^BS_Y)\quad\text{and}\quad(S_{X'}\theta^A)\circ(\lambda_{f'}g_A^{-1})\circ(f'^{-1}_B\lambda_g),$$
are classes of termwise maps of sheaf complexes that both send the inverse image of $q\otimes b$ to $h^{-1}f^{-1}q\otimes b$ under the canonical identification $f'^{-1}g^{-1}\cong h^{-1}f^{-1}$; since such local sections generate, the two maps of complexes coincide. This cube identity is an equality of natural transformations of functors $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\to D(X'_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$, before taking any mates.

proof.text: For R=A and R=B, the ambient exchange Ex^R is defined as the mate of the pullback composition isomorphism theta_square^R for the cartesian square. For every scheme map u, chi_u is by definition the mate of lambda_u under the two inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions. Thus the left composite in the claimed equality is the mate obtained by first taking the coefficient square for f and then the geometric exchange square, while the right composite is obtained by first taking the coefficient square for g and then the geometric exchange square. Their underlying left-adjoint composites are the two routes around the coefficient/pullback cube from Step 1.

source.place: Tag 0E47, remark-base-change and the definition of the base-change map as an adjoint

proof.text: Apply clause 1 (pasting along $G,H$) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] with $L_1=f_A^{-1}$, $L_2=f_B^{-1}$, $L_3=f'^{-1}_B$, $G=S_Y$, $H=S_X$, $G_2=g_B^{-1}$, $H_2=h_B^{-1}$, $\alpha=\lambda_f$, $\beta=\theta^B$: the square $(h_B^{-1}\lambda_f)\circ(\theta^BS_Y)$ has mate $(\operatorname{Ex}^BS_X)\circ(g_B^{-1}\chi_f)$. Apply the same clause with $L_1=f_A^{-1}$, $L_2=f'^{-1}_A$, $L_3=f'^{-1}_B$, $G=g_A^{-1}$, $H=h_A^{-1}$, $G_2=S_{Y'}$, $H_2=S_{X'}$, $\alpha=\theta^A$, $\beta=\lambda_{f'}$: the square $(S_{X'}\theta^A)\circ(\lambda_{f'}g_A^{-1})$ has mate $(\chi_{f'}h_A^{-1})\circ(S_{Y'}\operatorname{Ex}^A)$. Both computations are with respect to the adjunctions $f_A^{-1}\dashv Rf_*^A$ and $f'^{-1}_B\dashv Rf'^B_*$. Finally, from the component formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] and naturality of $\eta_2,\varepsilon_1$: for a square $\alpha:L_2G\to HL_1$ and transformations $\sigma:H\to H'$, $\tau:G'\to G$, the square $(\sigma L_1)\circ\alpha\circ(L_2\tau)$ has mate $(R_2\sigma)\circ\alpha^\flat\circ(\tau R_1)$. With $\sigma=\lambda_h$ this gives: the mate of the first composite of Step 1 is $Rf'^B_*(\lambda_h)\circ(\operatorname{Ex}^BS_X)\circ(g_B^{-1}\chi_f)$, the left side of the claim. With $\tau=\lambda_g$: the mate of the second composite of Step 1 is $(\chi_{f'}h_A^{-1})\circ(S_{Y'}\operatorname{Ex}^A)\circ(\lambda_gRf_*^A)$, the right side.

proof.text: By Step 1 the two squares $f'^{-1}_Bg_B^{-1}S_Y\to S_{X'}h_A^{-1}f_A^{-1}$ are equal, and the mate of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] is a function of the square (for the same functors $G=g_B^{-1}S_Y$, $H=S_{X'}h_A^{-1}$ and adjunctions), so by Step 3 their mates, the two sides of the claim evaluated at $M$, are equal. They are components of natural transformations, so the equality is natural in $M$. Only the K-flat computation of scalar extension, exactness of inverse images and the adjunction formalism were used; no properness, boundedness, constructibility, Tor-amplitude or flatness assumption on $A\to B$ enters.
